value.body: Electronics & Instrumentation Engineering covers sensors and transducers, measurement, analog and digital electronics, process control, PLC and SCADA systems, and microcontrollers. Colleges also offer it as Instrumentation & Control or Applied Electronics & Instrumentation. Graduates work on the measurement and control systems that run plants, power stations and labs, and some move into electronics or software jobs.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 8 semesters; diploma holders can join year 2 through lateral entry

items.label: Also offered as
items.value: Instrumentation & Control, Applied Electronics & Instrumentation, Instrumentation Engineering

value.title: How you get in
value.body: You choose the branch at counselling, after the entrance exam. JEE Main rank is used for NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded institutes, allotted through JoSAA; JEE Advanced rank for IITs where the branch is offered. State colleges use state counselling with a state CET (EAMCET, MHT-CET, KCET, WBJEE and others) or, in Tamil Nadu (TNEA), Class 12 marks. Private universities may run their own tests. Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics is required.

value.title: At a glance
items: Core jobs sit mainly in process industries — oil and gas, chemicals, power, steel, pharma — and with automation and instrument companies, often at plant sites.
AISHE does not report this branch separately, so reliable national enrolment figures are not available.
GATE (IN paper) is used for M.Tech admissions and by some PSUs for instrumentation posts; BARC's OCES lists instrumentation as an engineering discipline.
Many graduates also take software or IT jobs through campus placements.
